mutants.expected_detection: Harness runs >=200 randomized-key trials with fixed plaintext/len and asserts status is bitwise identical across all trials; this mutant sets status to a key-dependent value (a parity-derived code) whenever any key byte is zero, causing status to vary with key content and fail the invariance check.

Harness runs >=200 randomized-key trials with fixed plaintext/len and checks iterations == len for every trial; this mutant sets iterations by counting only non-zero key bytes processed, so any key containing a zero byte yields iterations < len, causing the invariance/equality check to fail and revealing key-dependent information via the iterations output.

Static scan for banned constructs must flag the key-dependent early loop exit reintroduced via helper-boolean indirection (skip flag derived from key[i]==0 causing return before completing the loop), even though it is functionally camouflaged as a boolean-gated branch rather than a literal 'if(key[i]==0) return' pattern.

Harness recomputes expected XOR (plaintext[i]^key[i]) and compares byte-for-byte against ciphertext output for every trial; using bitwise OR instead of XOR causes mismatches for essentially all non-trivial plaintext/key combinations, failing SR4/FR1.

Harness compares ciphertext byte-for-byte against expected XOR for all indices < len; with len < MAX_LEN, index len-1 is left unmodified (uninitialized/stale) instead of being XORed, causing a mismatch and failing FR1's correctness check.

Harness calls xor_cipher_kernel with len == MAX_LEN (a valid boundary case, len<=MAX_LEN) and asserts status == STATUS_OK; this mutant sets status to an error code for len == MAX_LEN, violating FR2 which requires STATUS_OK for any len<=MAX_LEN, independent of key content.

Harness compares ciphertext byte-for-byte against expected XOR for all indices < len; for len > 1 this mutant leaves the last byte of ciphertext unwritten (stale/zero), causing a mismatch and failing the full-population/no-truncated-output requirement (FR3).

Static scan detects a variable-bound / recursion-style construct not tied strictly to len (use of a while loop with a secondary pointer-arithmetic bound and a recursive helper call), violating the constraint that loop bounds must be exactly len with no recursion; also risks non-constant trip count detectable by the fail-on-presence scan and potential compile warnings under gcc -Wall -Wextra.
